_description: High-Entropy Alloy (HEA) composition sweep on BCC Fe structure. We explore how much Fe to substitute and in what ratios, keeping the BCC framework fixed.
_approach_explanation: PARTIAL SUBSTITUTION MODEL: In this model, the 'host' fraction represents the PERCENTAGE OF SITES TO SUBSTITUTE, not the final composition. For example, host={Fe: 0.35} with substitutional={Cr: 0.4, Ni: 0.4, Co: 0.2} means: 35% of all Fe sites are substituted. Of those substituted sites, 40% become Cr, 40% become Ni, 20% become Co. The remaining 65% of sites stay as Fe. This explores alloying by partially substituting the host element.
_workflow: 1) Start with pure BCC Fe (2 atoms/cell). 2) Scale to ~128 atoms. 3) For each substitution level (e.g., 35%, 45%, 55%), calculate how many sites to substitute. 4) Distribute those substituted sites among Cr/Ni/Co according to their ratios. 5) Generate random arrangements of the resulting composition.

host._comment: Percentage of Fe sites to substitute. 0.35 = 35% of all sites become substitutional

substitutional._comment: Ratios among substitutional elements. These must sum to 1.0 (they fill the substituted sites)

_note: Example: For N=150 atoms with Fe=0.35, Cr=0.4, Ni=0.4, Co=0.2: 35% of 150 = 52 sites substituted. These become 21 Cr + 21 Ni + 10 Co. Remaining 98 sites stay as Fe. Total: Fe98Cr21Ni21Co10 = 150 atoms.
